title: Hospital Bill Explained: Why You Pay $40 for One Aspirin
alts: Why Is Healthcare So Expensive in America? (Explained Simply)
Your Hospital Bill Is Fake. Here's How Prices Really Work.
line1: Why is your hospital bill so high? A $40 aspirin, secret negotiated prices and middlemen. Here's where the money goes, and how to fight back.
summary: Dave gets a few stitches and a month later a hospital bill with a $40 aspirin. We explain the hospital chargemaster and why list prices are mostly fake, the secret deals insurers negotiate (RAND: private plans pay ~254% of Medicare), the middlemen including insurers and pharmacy benefit managers (FTC findings), why the U.S. spends about twice as much per person as other rich countries (CMS, Peterson-KFF), surprise bills and the No Surprises Act, rising deductibles (KFF 2025), medical debt, and practical steps: itemized bills, negotiating, financial assistance and price transparency tools.
learn: What a hospital chargemaster is and why almost nobody pays list price
Why private insurance pays hospitals about 2.5x what Medicare pays (RAND)
How insurers and PBMs act as middlemen in your healthcare costs
Why the U.S. spends ~$15,000 per person, about double other rich countries
Your rights under the No Surprises Act and how deductibles really work
